races.name: Michael Maine Memorial Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Tomarlo
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces traffic concerns in 9-runner field, 32 days off but shown improvement for new yard recently.
runners_data.comment: Well backed for new yard latest, when things didn't pan out his way; on an attractive mark
runners_data.spotlight: A fair ex-Irish 6f winner; offered little in three runs for Barry Brennan early in 2026 but much more positive signs for new yard with fourth of eight in 5f Wolverhampton handicap last month, keeping on late after tardy start; a bold showing is on the cards eased 1lb.

runners_data.name: Call Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer well-placed to track So Smart but 62 days off suggests fitness query despite being race-fit.
runners_data.comment: Both wins on soft ground; probably best to leave him alone until he gets his conditions.
runners_data.spotlight: Doubled his career tally over C&D in September; off five months and shaped as if in need of the run when a fading tenth of 13 in 5f Bath handicap on his return in April; can take a step forward.

runners_data.name: So Smart
runners_data.note: Natural pace-setter with excellent recent C&D form, 8 days since last run ideal and will dictate terms from the front.
runners_data.comment: Didn't run badly over C&D last week and Ashley Lewis claims his useful 5lb today
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner who arrives in decent nick, leading long way when third of five over C&D eight days ago; must enter calculations off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Fletcher's Flight
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on long losing streak, went too keen in cheekpieces last time which may be repeated here.
runners_data.comment: Unseated when rearing at start on stable debut; first-time cheekpieces go on; best watched
runners_data.spotlight: On a long losing run and he went too freely in first-time cheekpieces for his new yard when a below-par fourth of eight in 5f Lingfield handicap 18 days ago; tongue tied now with more required.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up racer with strong C&D record, recent Bath third suggests return to form but needs luck in running.
runners_data.spotlight: A three-time C&D scorer (twice last summer) and this veteran got back on track with third of seven in 5.5f Bath handicap 25 days ago; a likely player eased 1lb returned here.

runners_data.name: Hidden Verse
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with C&D win last summer, solid recent Bath run but must overcome wide draw and traffic issues.
runners_data.spotlight: Scored twice last summer (including over C&D) and comes here on the back of a solid fifth in 5.5f Bath handicap 25 days ago; not out of things from an easing mark.

runners_data.name: Son Of Astar
runners_data.note: Former 5f winner now without headgear after poor recent form, hold-up style faces usual traffic concerns.
runners_data.comment: Has dropped to a competitive mark but slight query tackling 6f again; headgear absent
runners_data.spotlight: A three-time 5f winner in 2025; yet to hit top form this season though, going without headgear after three months off when last of 12 in 6f handicap here 16 days ago; blinkers return but he needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Macarone
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for new yard but disappointing debut for stable, needs significant improvement to feature.
runners_data.comment: Acts with ease in the ground and nothing wrong with this mark ahead of his stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 6f scorer for Ivan Furtado in 2025; changed hands for 2,000gns before coming in just tenth for new yard in 6f handicap here 16 days ago; needs to take a big step forward.

runners_data.name: Pearl's Edge
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 210 days off showing poor late-2025 form, looks outclassed here.
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo who ended 2025 well below par; back from seven months off with plenty more required.

races.paceDynamic: So Smart will set the pace from Call Time and Macarone, with the confirmed front-runner likely to get an easy lead given the lack of natural speed in this field. The moderate early gallop will see the large group of hold-up horses (Tomarlo, Fletcher's Flight, Some Nightmare, Hidden Verse, Son Of Astar, Pearl's Edge) tracking behind in a bunched pack. With So Smart able to dictate terms uncontested, this race shape strongly favours the pace-setter and prominent racers who can travel into contention early, as the hold-up brigade will face a wall of horses when trying to make their moves in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: So Smart controls completely
scenarios.trigger: If So Smart gets uncontested fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The pace-setter will have too much in reserve after an easy lead, with Call Time best placed to chase but unlikely to reel in the leader. Hold-up horses face traffic problems and give the winner too much start.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pair battle
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time and Macarone press So Smart early creating moderate pace
scenarios.body: The three-way speed battle will set up a finish between the prominent racers, with So Smart's class edge proving decisive late. Early positioning becomes crucial as the backmarkers struggle for racing room.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closer strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a crawl throughout
scenarios.body: Some Nightmare and Hidden Verse can exploit their turn of foot in a sprint finish, with the veteran's course experience proving valuable. The pace-setters will have too little pace early to build a winning advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If the main fancies underperform and the pace becomes messy
scenarios.body: Son Of Astar or Fletcher's Flight can capitalize on a muddled affair where class horses fail to fire. Traffic problems affect the favourites while a fresher horse finds a clear passage late.

watchPoints.text: So Smart could get dangerously easy fractions if Call Time and Macarone don't press early enough
Some Nightmare and Hidden Verse both need clear runs in straight as hold-up horses in small field
Son Of Astar running without headgear after three months off suggests connections expecting improved effort
Fletcher's Flight may race too keenly again in cheekpieces having gone too freely last time
Call Time's fitness after 62-day break will show early if struggling to keep pace with So Smart

races.name: LSL Racing Horse Sales Syndication Leasing/EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive)

runners_data.name: Big Hitter
runners_data.comment: February foal by Starspangledbanner; 65,000euros yearling; paper appeal so watch betting
runners_data.spotlight: 65,000euros yearling; dam 6f 2yo winner (Group 2; RPR 100), half-sister to winners Oliver Hardy (1m2f/1m4f) and Dajla (Spanish 1m-1m3f), out of a maiden sister to 6f/7f 2yo Group 2 winner Strategic Prince; this Starspangledbanner filly needs considering, especially if the market vibes are positive.

runners_data.name: Secret Rival
runners_data.spotlight: 60,000gns yearling; dam 5f 2yo winner (RPR 85), half-sister to 5f winners Orlaith (Listed) and Tammy Wynette, out of an unraced half-sister to 7f 2yo Group 1 winner Toormore; this Ardad filly appeals on paper and must enter calculations for good yard.

runners_data.name: Angels Lane
runners_data.spotlight: 27,000gns yearling; Harry Angel filly; half-sister to 5f/5.5f winner Supersonic Man (Australia; RPR 88); dam unraced sister to 7.3f winner One Kiss, half-sister to 6f Group 3 winner Jimmy Styles; the market can guide for this debutante.

runners_data.name: Chilli
runners_data.spotlight: Harry Angel filly; dam 8.6f 2yo winner (RPR 77), sister to 1m5f winner Isaiah; the betting can prove an accurate indicator.

runners_data.name: Clueisinthetitle
runners_data.spotlight: 22,000gns yearling; half-sister to 7f/1m winner Lambournghini (RPR 54); dam Listed-placed 5f 2yo winner (RPR 93), sister to Listed-placed 6f 2yo winner Pastoral Girl; yard's juveniles are going well so this Ubettabelieveit filly is very much one to consider.

runners_data.name: Penny Capri
runners_data.comment: £50,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; by Minzaal; wears hood on debut; check the betting
runners_data.spotlight: 11-1 and hooded, hinted at promise with sixth of ten in maiden at Chester (5.5f, good) on her first run 30 days ago, leading until 1f out; this Minzaal filly can build on it here.

runners_data.name: My Maria
runners_data.comment: 50,000gns breeze-up 2yo; half-sister to two sprint winners; yard's 2yos going well
runners_data.spotlight: 9-2, shaped with encouragement when a debut fourth of nine in novice at Salisbury (5f, good) two weeks ago, keeping on late having been hampered over 2f out; this daughter of Persian Force seems sure to take a step forward.

runners_data.name: Miss Moneypit
runners_data.spotlight: Without Parole filly; built on debut promise with keeping-on fourth of 12 in 5f Ascot novice last month; she looks to have more to offer over 6f so merits serious consideration.

runners_data.name: Resemblance
runners_data.spotlight: Bayside Boy filly who took a big step forward from her debut when a clear second of nine in 6f Haydock maiden 15 days ago; she holds very good form claims.

races.name: Capital Windscreens Supporting Breast Cancer Handicap

runners_data.name: Island Bear
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader who gets blinkers for first time after disappointing Nottingham fifth, 18 days gap should have him spot-on
runners_data.comment: May do better returned to turf in this second handicap attempt
runners_data.spotlight: Fair maiden who wasn't discredited with fifth of nine in 1m Nottingham handicap 18 days ago; not out of things eased 1lb with blinkers added.

runners_data.name: Poetry Of Time
runners_data.note: Front runner with class advantage after comfortable Salisbury win, gelded over winter and William Haggas yard in good form
runners_data.spotlight: In the frame all four starts as a 2yo; gelded and comfortably off the mark in 7f Salisbury novice on his return last month; this son of Ulysses has more to offer now handicapping; major player.

runners_data.name: Mighty Vega
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent form with recent Lingfield turf success, up 3lb but consistent type who handles conditions
runners_data.comment: Being kept busy on the AW, but anyone's guess how he will cope with the return to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Enjoyed a very good winter on the AW and he gained a first turf win in 7f Lingfield handicap 11 days ago; up 3lb but this consistent sort can go well again.

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 7-month break with encouraging Wolverhampton fourth, well-weighted on 127lbs
runners_data.comment: Won a Lingfield maiden last August before being turned over in three handicaps.
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 7f winner as 2yo; resumed from seven months off with a good fourth of seven in 8.5f handicap at Wolverhampton 19 days ago; she's very much one to consider eased 1lb.

runners_data.name: Electrical
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who hasn't progressed since debut win, gelded before disappointing handicap return and 42 days off track
runners_data.spotlight: Made a winning debut in 6f Newbury novice last July; has failed to kick on in three runs since though, gelded before beating only one on his handicap debut/return at Haydock (1m) in April; has something to prove.

runners_data.name: Aigeas
runners_data.note: Front runner with early speed but concerning pattern of fading in finish, gelded since poor Leicester return
runners_data.spotlight: Debut scorer at Deauville (6.5f) in October but well below that form both subsequent runs, 11th of 13 in 6f Leicester novice on his return in April; since gelded and needs to take a big step forward on his handicap debut with hood/tongue-tie also added.

runners_data.name: Ebn Sabt
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping down in trip after Lingfield win, 65 days absence and blinkers applied for stable debut
runners_data.comment: Has somewhat regressed since winning at Lingfield in first-time blinkers
runners_data.spotlight: Gained a first win at Lingfield (1m) in February but he ended his time with William Muir and Chris Grassick with a below-par seventh in 1m Southwell handicap in April; since changed hands for 7,000gns and needs to bounce back for new trainer.

races.paceDynamic: Poetry Of Time, Island Bear, and Aigeas will ensure a strong gallop from the start with all three confirmed front runners likely to go forward early. The sustained pace over 7f on soft ground will test stamina reserves, particularly as Poetry Of Time and Island Bear have the class to maintain pressure throughout. Aigeas has shown a tendency to fade in the finish which could leave the other two to battle it out, creating a searching test for the field. This pace setup strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can finish strongly, while the confirmed leaders may pay for their early exertions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Poetry Of Time and Island Bear go toe-to-toe early while Aigeas fades as usual
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will set up perfectly for Mighty Vega and Lyra Lea to pick up the pieces, with Ebn Sabt also benefiting from his hold-up style. The leaders will have done too much work on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Poetry Of Time Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Poetry Of Time can break clear of Island Bear and control the tempo from the front
scenarios.body: His class edge and recent gelding operation could see him dictate terms and prove too strong, with Mighty Vega best placed to chase him home. The Haggas runner has winning form fresh and looks the one to beat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders cancel each other out early allowing the race to develop tactically
scenarios.body: Electrical and Lyra Lea could benefit from a steadier pace that plays to their prominent racing styles. The reduced early pace would nullify the closers' advantage and favour those who can travel and quicken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Island Bear Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Island Bear can improve significantly from his Nottingham fifth with the addition of blinkers
scenarios.body: The headgear change and 1lb drop in weight could spark improvement, while his front-running style suits if he can find more than recent form suggests. This remains the least likely outcome given his moderate recent efforts.

watchPoints.text: Poetry Of Time could prove too classy if allowed to dictate terms from the front without serious pressure
Island Bear with first-time blinkers might show significant improvement from recent moderate form
Mighty Vega's consistency and recent turf win make him the danger if the pace collapses
Aigeas has early speed but watch for signs of his usual late fade developing
Ebn Sabt is shortest trip for 65 days but his hold-up style suits if the pace is strong enough

races.name: Late Arron James Supporting Pancreatic Cancer Handicap

runners_data.name: Racingbreaks Ryder
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 221-day break but showed ability over course and distance when third last time out
runners_data.spotlight: Went winless in 2025 but he posted some good placed efforts, signing off with a solid third in 1m Leicester handicap in October; not out of it if fully tuned up for his seasonal return so worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Kisskodi
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up performer with recent course form, ideally placed to benefit from strong early pace
runners_data.comment: May resume progress with AW reappearance under his belt; should take well to Goodwood
runners_data.spotlight: Progressed well in 2025 when a four-time winner at 6f/7f; has gone with promise on both starts this spring, suffering a poor run before staying on into fifth of 14 at Goodwood (7f) 15 days ago; can race off a 1lb lower mark here so a bold showing is on the cards.

runners_data.name: Bold Impact
runners_data.note: Struggling since yard switch but hold-up style suits likely pace scenario, though form remains a concern
runners_data.comment: Resurgent over 6f at Windsor last time; step back up in trip promises to suit
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 7f scorer for Ralph Beckett in 2024; yet to match that form for his current yard, though not disgraced when seventh in 1m Windsor handicap 12 days ago; possibilities from a falling mark.

runners_data.name: Under The Twilight
runners_data.note: Honest mare dropping 2lb in handicap mark with proven ability to pick up pieces from off the pace
runners_data.comment: Her last two wins have come over C&D, the latest off this mark last June; each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: On a losing run but she arrives in good nick, fourth of nine in 6f Windsor handicap 26 days ago; she ought to be thereabouts once more off a 2lb lower mark.

runners_data.name: This Farh
runners_data.note: In-form prominent runner stepping up from recent victories, though rising handicap mark poses challenge
runners_data.comment: Leicester 7f win last month; 6f probably explains a lesser show last time
runners_data.spotlight: In fine form since returned to turf this spring, winning at Leicester (7f, good) in April and at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) ten days ago; up another 3lb but this gutsy front-runner is a likely player once more.

runners_data.name: Terries Royale
runners_data.note: Front-running veteran on long losing sequence, cheekpieces applied to sharpen focus from the gates
runners_data.comment: Said to have been unsuited by Chepstow's undulations last time; this is easier down 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: On a lengthy losing sequence and he failed to beat a rival in 8.5f Wolverhampton handicap five days ago; cheekpieces are retried now.

runners_data.name: Dapper Gee Gee
runners_data.note: Course winner last time who can track early pace before finishing strongly, form working out well
runners_data.comment: AW winner under Gina Mangan in January; fair fourth latest; claims
runners_data.spotlight: Gained a second C&D victory when getting up late in 11-runner handicap last month; up 2lb but that form is working out well so he must enter calculations.

runners_data.name: Slipper Time
runners_data.note: Showed early promise but concerning recent runs suggest confidence issues, needs to settle better
runners_data.comment: Disappointing upped to 1m at Kempton final 3yo start but he's bred to stay;  lightly raced
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark in 7f Salisbury novice in August but failed to beat a rival at Kempton on his final run in 2025 and went freely when beating one on his return in 1m Newmarket handicap last month; needs to become more tractable.

runners_data.name: Connie's Rose
runners_data.note: Course specialist front runner dropping in trip, tongue-tie applied after narrow defeat eight days ago
runners_data.comment: Close third over C&D last week; back in action before 1lb nudge takes effect; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Course specialist who just missed out on an eighth course victory when beaten a neck over C&D eight days ago; very much one to consider despite a 2lb rise.

runners_data.name: Brave Byreflection
runners_data.note: Disappointing since trainer switch, prominent style suits but lacks recent form evidence
runners_data.spotlight: C&D scorer for Alice Haynes last July; yet to fire for her new yard though in 1m handicaps at Kempton and Southwell in April; lots more is required.

runners_data.name: Receipt
runners_data.note: Won last completed start but raced too keenly when fading badly at Kempton, pace concerns remain
runners_data.comment: Again inclined to hang right but won easily on handicap debut last week (Tapeta); player
runners_data.spotlight: Made a winning start in handicaps at Southwell (7f) in April but he raced very keenly when beating just two in 7f Kempton handicap the following month; still low mileage so shouldn't be written off on his Flat turf debut.

runners_data.name: Bela Sonata
runners_data.note: Front runner whose form has declined significantly, struggling to recapture winning form from early 2025
runners_data.spotlight: A dual 7f winner in first half of 2025; hasn't returned in much form though, beating only one in 7f AW Lingfield handicap 25 days ago; hard to make a case for.

races.paceDynamic: Terries Royale, Receipt, Connie's Rose and Bela Sonata will all be sent forward from the gates, creating a fierce early gallop over 7f at Chepstow. Receipt has shown tendencies to race keenly and fade, while Connie's Rose is a course specialist who will look to dominate from the front. The strong early pace will stretch the field and test stamina reserves on the soft ground. This aggressive tempo clearly favours hold-up horses who can pick off tiring leaders in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the four front runners engage in a speed duel through the first half-mile.
scenarios.body: The leaders will come back to the field dramatically in the final two furlongs, allowing closers with tactical speed to surge past tired pace-setters. Hold-up specialists like Kisskodi and Under The Twilight benefit most from this energy-sapping scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Connie's Rose or Dapper Gee Gee can steal a soft lead while others fight.
scenarios.body: The winner will dictate fractions and have enough left to repel late challenges, using course knowledge or proven tactical nous to maximum advantage. Prominent runners who can vary their pace hold the key in this moderate tempo scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If all four leaders maintain their positions without destructive early fractions.
scenarios.body: The pace will be honest but not suicidal, creating a genuine staying test where horses with proven 7f form can battle out a competitive finish. This scenario suits horses with both early speed and stamina reserves on testing ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders go too fast and multiple horses stop quickly.
scenarios.body: The race will develop into a sprint finish between whatever horses remain with energy, likely creating a blanket finish. Late-running outsiders and horses returning from breaks could benefit from this chaotic development.

watchPoints.text: Receipt and Terries Royale could engage in a destructive early speed battle that compromises both horses' chances
Slipper Time may race too freely again given his tendency to pull hard in competitive handicaps
Connie's Rose's tongue-tie application suggests connections are addressing breathing issues after recent near-miss
This Farh carries a 3lb penalty for recent Beverley success but arrives in peak form
Bela Sonata's recent poor form makes him vulnerable despite prominent early position

races.name: V3 UK- Principal Contractor Handicap (Chepstow Mile Series Qualifier) (Div I)

runners_data.name: Fifty Sent
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 49-day break with inconsistent recent form but won twice at Southwell in March
runners_data.comment: Record of 1-18 on turf and was a well-held fourth at Nottingham latest; down the list
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form when winning two classified events at Southwell (1m) in March but he's been well held back in handicaps in his last two runs; didn't run badly at Nottingham (8.3f, good) in April but that took his turf record to 1-18.

runners_data.name: Saturnalia
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in freefall form, last of 11 at Bath and hasn't won since 2023 on all-weather
runners_data.comment: Chance on last year's best but he ended 2025 quietly; amateur takes her first rules ride
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins came on AW in 2023 when trained by Richard Hughes; has gone into freefall since and was last of 11 at Bath last month.

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with multiple placings last year, 10-year-old experience could be valuable in traffic
runners_data.spotlight: Some fair efforts on the AW during the winter and he was placed on multiple occasions last year; ran okay at Bath (1m, good to soft) in April but he's without a win since August 2023.

runners_data.name: Fitzmaurice
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse down to basement mark but 12-race maiden struggling for competitiveness this year
runners_data.comment: Down to a basement mark but 0-11 and struggling to get competitive this year
runners_data.spotlight: Down to a basement mark but this 12-race maiden has been struggling to get competitive this year and others make greater appeal.

runners_data.name: Praise Indeed
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 324-day layoff making handicap debut, fades in finish historically
runners_data.spotlight: Three modest runs last summer when trained by Tom Ward; has switched yards since and makes handicap debut; needs to overcome lengthy absence but she may have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Liberty Bird
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse has lost form since leaving Charlie Johnston, pulled up bleeding last time at Windsor
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins came in 2024 when trained by Charlie Johnston; has lost her form and now with her third trainer since; pulled up at Windsor last time (bled from the nose).

runners_data.name: Judge Frank
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with natural exuberance, both recent wins came in September 2024, key pace angle
runners_data.comment: No wins since September 2024 and doesn't appear to be crying out for another go at 1m2f
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins came in September 2024; tends to race prominently and if his natural exuberance can be harnessed then he would not be far away.

runners_data.name: Mooretown Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse tumbled down weights since British debut, tends to be hostage to fortune tactically
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came in August 2024 when trained in Ireland; has tumbled down the weights since his British debut in December; is a hostage to fortune as he tends to be held up and requires a fast pace to be seen to best effect.

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping up in trip with 5lb claiming jockey, best effort was third here last September
runners_data.comment: Encouraging third in C&D maiden (soft) but beaten 10l in two handicaps; still early days
runners_data.spotlight: Best effort when third here in a maiden (6f, soft) last September; well held in three handicaps since; steps up in trip and needs to show improvement.

runners_data.name: Scarfo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse long time since sole win, hard to make case with poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Long time since his sole win and hasn't offered much this year; hard to make a case for
runners_data.spotlight: Long time since his sole win and hasn't offered much this year; hard to make a case for.

races.paceDynamic: Judge Frank will make the early running in this 10-runner handicap, with Eye Of The Water likely to race handy behind him. With no other natural front-runners, Judge Frank should get an uncontested lead and set a steady tempo on the good to soft ground. The large field of hold-up horses including Fifty Sent, Saturnalia, Fitzmaurice, and Mooretown Lad will be looking for gaps in the home straight. This race shape heavily favours prominent racers and front-runners who can avoid the traffic problems that will inevitably develop when multiple hold-up horses try to make their moves simultaneously.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Judge Frank gets an easy lead and conserves energy early
scenarios.body: Judge Frank will have too much in reserve for the hold-up horses who face a wall of traffic in the straight. The prominent racer can kick for home when the pace lifts and hold off late challenges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large contingent of hold-up horses all hit traffic problems simultaneously
scenarios.body: Multiple runners will be hampered seeking room, allowing a horse that gets first run to capitalize. The race will become a lottery with positioning crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Judge Frank goes too fast early and compounds on the testing ground
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses will have a target to aim at as the leader tires markedly in the final furlong. Those with the best finishing kicks will prevail.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Eye Of The Water tracks Judge Frank perfectly and times his challenge ideally
scenarios.body: The 10-year-old can use his experience to position perfectly behind the leader before striking. His recent consistent form gives him the edge over less reliable rivals.

watchPoints.text: Judge Frank to get uncontested lead - if opposed early he could compound on testing ground
Traffic problems in home straight with seven hold-up horses seeking same gaps simultaneously
Liberty Bird's breathing issues after bleeding last time could resurface under pressure
Eye Of The Water's positioning behind Judge Frank will determine if he can time challenge correctly
Fifty Sent's fitness after 49-day break when needing to produce finishing kick from rear

races.name: V3 UK- Principal Contractor Handicap (Chepstow Mile Series Qualifier) (Div II)

runners_data.name: Prince Ali
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist but all six wins came on AW surfaces and cheekpieces return after 32 days off
runners_data.spotlight: All six wins have been on AW; cheekpieces return but he doesn't convince.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse who rarely wins but makes the frame regularly, 8 days since last run keeps him sharp
runners_data.comment: Slightly disappointing on recent turf return but was in good form on AW beforehand
runners_data.spotlight: Generally consistent but doesn't win too often; hasn't been far away of late and regularly makes the frame; has place claims.

runners_data.name: Homeland
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 187 days off, previously won off 5lb higher mark but stable form concerning at 0/6
runners_data.comment: Turf winner for Michael Dods; held by The Dark Baron on C&D running last time
runners_data.spotlight: Scored for Michael Dods at Ripon (1m2f, good) last July off 5lb higher; sold to join current yard for 4,000gns in October; fifth of 12 on stable debut at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) in December; unraced since but on a decent mark.

runners_data.name: Rival
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but hasn't won since September 2022 and 285-day layoff raises fitness doubts
runners_data.spotlight: Last of two wins came in September 2022; seemed to find his level again last year when making the frame four times; has been absent since last August though and needs to hit the ground running.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose mark has dropped significantly, building on April's improved fifth at Nottingham
runners_data.comment: Losing run goes back to July 2024 but on a reduced mark; non-runner 5:18 Redcar yesterday
runners_data.spotlight: His losing run goes back to July 2024 and his mark has plummeted since but he could build on April's fifth at Nottingham; not discounted.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Sunrise
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden but showed best form when beaten a nose at Kempton in January, needs to transfer AW form to turf
runners_data.comment: Went very close over C&D in January and is a big player if he can repeat that form
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-race maiden but has shown he can find a race; best effort was when beaten a nose at Kempton (1m, AW) in January and if can replicate that form on turf then he comes into the equation; has left Pat Phelan since his last run in March; sports a first-time tongue-tie and has to be of interest for new yard.

runners_data.name: Nutcracker
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden who has improved in recent classified events at Wolverhampton but faces tougher handicap company
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden but has gone close in classified events at Wolverhampton (8.5, AW) on his last two starts; needs to convert that form to handicaps on turf.

runners_data.name: Marisitta
runners_data.note: Inconsistent hold-up maiden with cheekpieces returning, hard to trust despite dropping in grade
runners_data.comment: Chance of getting off the mark largely depends on how well she responds to hood
runners_data.spotlight: Still a maiden and lacks consistency to boot; returning cheekpieces replace first-time hood worn last time; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Uncle Albert
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making British debut with concerning tendency to fade in finish, probably needs this run
runners_data.comment: Continues to drop in the ratings, well treated on old form, a top apprentice booked
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came in March 2024 when trained by Kieran Cotter in Ireland; has lost his way this year and makes his British/stable debut; probably best watched for now.

races.paceDynamic: Homeland will set the early tempo as the sole confirmed front runner, likely joined by Rival in the prominent positions given his P-style. With only one dedicated pace-setter in a small field of nine, this sets up for a modest, sustainable gallop that won't stretch the field significantly. The lack of early pressure means Homeland can dictate terms without being harried, allowing the large pack of hold-up horses (Prince Ali, King Of The Dance, Charencey, Whiskey Sunrise, Nutcracker, Marisitta, Uncle Albert) to settle and deliver their challenges late. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can quicken off the steady tempo, with prominent runners also well-placed to capitalize on the uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains modest as expected with Homeland controlling the tempo uncontested
scenarios.body: The large contingent of hold-up horses will have every chance to close strongly up the rail and through the pack. Late-finishing types like King Of The Dance and Charencey benefit most from the sustainable gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Homeland and Rival establish a clear advantage and neither fades in the testing ground
scenarios.body: The two prominent runners maintain their position advantage as the hold-up brigade struggles to make up significant ground on the soft surface. Homeland's fresher legs could prove decisive having been off since August.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Kick Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one hold-up horse produces a superior turn of foot in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: A horse with genuine acceleration like Whiskey Sunrise or the returning Uncle Albert could exploit the steady pace with a devastating late surge. The tactical advantage of racing from behind proves crucial on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Homeland is left completely alone on the lead and maintains stamina reserves
scenarios.body: With no early pressure whatsoever, Homeland could simply steal a march and hold on as the closers arrive too late. The 187-day layoff becomes a positive as fresh legs outbattle tired finishers.

watchPoints.text: Uncle Albert shows tendency to fade in finish and makes stable debut - watch for any early market support
Homeland has been off for 187 days and trainer Thomas Faulkner is 0/6 in last 14 days - fitness could be lacking
Watch early pace as Homeland may go off too fast if challenged by Rival, potentially setting up stronger finishers
Several hold-up horses like Prince Ali and Whiskey Sunrise need to prove AW form transfers to testing turf conditions
Charencey's much-reduced handicap mark could make him well-handicapped if recapturing July 2024 winning form

races.name: Capital Windscreens Supporting Autistic Society Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaleidoscope Eyes
runners_data.note: Front runner with class but 229 days off and needs to prove fitness against these after beating just one last time out
runners_data.spotlight: Opened his account for current yard at Ffos Las (7f) in September but off since beating one in 7f Wolverhampton handicap following month; needs to hit the ground running on his seasonal return.

runners_data.name: Be An Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who goes well fresh but hasn't raced since May and can be difficult to settle
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Leicester (6f) last May but she didn't prove the easiest to catch right later in 2025; has gone well fresh though, so not out of things on her seasonal return.

runners_data.name: Margorie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won at Windsor but struggled since going handicapping, including poor effort here 16 days ago
runners_data.comment: No impact in handicaps since soft-ground maiden win but going may be more in favour now
runners_data.spotlight: Gained a first win at Windsor (6f) in September but she has failed to build on it since handicapping, ninth of 11 over 7f here 16 days ago; mark is falling but she still needs to take a big step forward.

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent current form with second at Brighton eight days ago, well positioned off unchanged mark
runners_data.comment: 0-19; competitive but this first visit to Brighton needs to spark something extra from him
runners_data.spotlight: 0-20 but he arrives in good nick, second of 13 in 6f Brighton handicap eight days ago; well in the mix again off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Autumn Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won course and distance 16 days ago without usual headgear, up 3lb but must be respected
runners_data.spotlight: Had usual headgear left off when ending a long losing sequence over C&D 16 days ago; up 3lb but must enter calculations.

runners_data.name: Sub Thirteen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has struggled this season for new trainer Jeremy Scott, 13th of 14 at Windsor two weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 6f scorer for Tony Carroll but largely below par this season for his present handler, 13th of 14 in 6f Windsor handicap two weeks ago; others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Ravenglass
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and course winner who needs to build on encouraging reappearance fourth, tries blinkers for first time
runners_data.comment: Failed to shine latest but promising reappearance previously; races off last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner last May; has twice failed to build on an encouraging reappearance fourth at Wolverhampton in April so more is required here in a change of headgear.

runners_data.name: The Bear Of Saints
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making first start in 640 days for new trainer after being gelded, fitness major concern
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden; not disgraced with fifth in 5.6f Bath maiden on his final run for Joe Tickle in September 2024; since gelded and has his fitness to prove on his comeback run for a new yard.

runners_data.name: Snuggle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 10-month break but shaped encouragingly fourth here 16 days ago for new stable
runners_data.comment: Two 6f wins; market might help on stable debut (same owner) and first run for ten months
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 6f scorer for Luke Dace in 2024; off ten months but shaped well for his new stable with fourth of 12 in C&D handicap 16 days ago; not without interest off a reduced mark.

runners_data.name: Punchbowl Flyer
runners_data.note: Front runner and dual course winner whose form has declined, beaten all but one at Wolverhampton last time
runners_data.comment: In good form at 6f and 7f here in the spring but may have gone off the boil now
runners_data.spotlight: Dual C&D scorer but his good form has dipped of late, beating only one at Wolverhampton (7f) last time; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Diamondsinthesand
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and three-time winner in 2025 but yet to fire in three runs this season
runners_data.comment: His last win was at Bath (5.6f) but he's finished down the field there in last three runs
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time winner (around 6f) in 2025 but he's yet to hit top form in a trio of runs this season, seventh of 13 at Nottingham (5f) 18 days ago.

runners_data.name: Too Much Trevor
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse still seeking first win but arrives in good form with third over 7f here eight days ago
runners_data.comment: 0-29 but went close over C&D last week and is effectively 4lb lower today
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to score in 30 attempts but she comes here in decent nick, third of ten in 7f handicap here eight days ago; back up 4lb now, though.

races.paceDynamic: Kaleidoscope Eyes and Punchbowl Flyer will force the early pace, with Kaleidoscope Eyes the more reliable front runner despite his 229-day absence. Five runners (Be An Angel, On Key, Autumn Angel, The Bear Of Saints, Snuggle) want prominent positions creating congestion through the first three furlongs. The hold-up brigade of Margorie, Sub Thirteen, Ravenglass, Diamondsinthesand and Too Much Trevor will track behind but face traffic problems in the closing stages on Chepstow's tight 6f circuit. This pace dynamic strongly favours prominent runners who can secure clean positions early and avoid the squeeze.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace setters create honest fractions without going too fast
scenarios.body: The prominent runners can track comfortably and kick clear before the hold-up horses get organised. Autumn Angel and On Key benefit most from their tactical speed and current form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Kaleidoscope Eyes and Punchbowl Flyer go too fast early given their fitness concerns
scenarios.body: The pace collapses allowing the best hold-up horse to sweep through late. Too Much Trevor's recent third here gives him the edge over the other closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Kaleidoscope Eyes Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If the class leader finds his old speed despite the long layoff
scenarios.body: His superior ability on his day allows him to dictate from the front and hold on grimly. Punchbowl Flyer's declining form makes him vulnerable despite similar tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners get caught in traffic and the leaders fold
scenarios.body: A horse coming from further back with a clear run can capitalise on the carnage. Sub Thirteen or The Bear Of Saints could benefit from the tactical breakdown.

watchPoints.text: Kaleidoscope Eyes faces major fitness test after 229 days off and if he doesn't handle the pace-forcing role, front running collapses entirely
Traffic problems are inevitable with five prominent runners fighting for position on Chepstow's tight track, watch for interference 2-3 furlongs out
Punchbowl Flyer's declining form makes him unreliable as pace partner, if he doesn't contribute early fractions become messy
Too Much Trevor drops back to 6f after running well over 7f here last time and the shorter trip should suit her closing kick
The Bear Of Saints returns after 640 days off and if showing early pace his fitness will become apparent quickly

races.name: Capital Windscreens Supporting Mental Health Handicap

runners_data.name: Electric Bass
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form who should get an ideal stalking position behind the uncontested leader
runners_data.spotlight: 0-13 and his six runner-up placings may suggest something's afoot; did dead-heat at Kempton (1m4f, AW; demoted to second) in November and he comes here in form having chased one home again at Southwell in April and Bath last time; handles good to soft; can make his presence felt.

runners_data.name: Port Of Entry
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced prominent type making only second start for new connections after 33-day break
runners_data.comment: Out of the frame in six starts, including on stable debut over C&D four weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Very lightly raced ex-French 6yo who didn't set the world alight for Andre Fabre in 2023, and after a fairly encouraging comeback for this yard at Kempton in April he was tailed off back there (also 2m, AW) one month later; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Baileys Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from a 243-day absence with poor recent form before the break
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winning mare (2m, AW) but she was running poorly when last seen in the autumn; nothing wrong with this mark if the break has recharged her batteries but this is a rare turf outing and probably doesn't want too much rain.

runners_data.name: Bug Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran with excellent course record including two wins at this trip, returning from 266-day layoff
runners_data.comment: Just one run last year when beaten 15l in September; hard to know what to expect this time
runners_data.spotlight: Good record here down the years, with form figures of 21319 highlighting two wins at 1m4f (good); also scored twice over this trip in 2023 (including on good to soft) but no wins since and he only saw the track once last year; still worth a market check ahead of his return.

runners_data.name: Cloudside Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good current form with recent wins at Ffos Las and Southwell over similar trips
runners_data.spotlight: Took ten goes to get off the mark but it was a convincing win at Ffos Las (1m4f, soft) in August and he doubled his tally when bagging Southwell handicap (1m3f, AW) on his April return; back up 4lb but he might be capable of better and holds leading claims.

runners_data.name: Marinakis
runners_data.note: Hold-up type on lowest weight but making only second start for new trainer Robert Stephens
runners_data.comment: All three wins have been on AW and has claims if he can revive back on Polytrack
runners_data.spotlight: Generally consistent in his time with Ian Williams when he scored three times on AW from 1m to 1m2f; second start for this yard wasn't devoid of promise at Kempton (1m4f) 17 days ago but suitability for the combination of this trip and likely ground is yet to be determined.

runners_data.name: Big Win
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with recent second at Bath, could press the leader if needed
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced at two; just five starts for Harry Charlton and following 18,000gns sale it was a good start for these connections when second at Bath (1m6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; likely softer ground is an unknown but he attracted support ahead of that stable debut and should cope with this drop back in trip; player.

runners_data.name: Rosco Rogers
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching from all-weather to turf for first time with modest recent efforts
runners_data.spotlight: AW campaigner who is having his first realistic go on turf; went close at Wolverhampton (9.5f) and Kempton (1m4f) in his first two handicaps but didn't progress across this winter's campaign; last two starts saw big defeats in the spring but maybe wind surgery will help and a tongue-tie is now added to his cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Wonderful Wendy
runners_data.note: Front runner getting first handicap start who should get uncontested lead in small field
runners_data.spotlight: Withdrawn from her intended debut last July on account of soft ground; modest form in three qualifying runs from 1m2f to 1m4f (AW/good) but starts her handicapping career at a modest level and no surprise if she can do better in this sphere; heed any market signals.

races.paceDynamic: Wonderful Wendy provides the only confirmed pace angle as the sole front runner, giving her an uncontested lead in a small field of nine. Electric Bass and Port Of Entry will sit prominent behind her, while Big Win could also press forward early. The pace will be moderate and sustainable with limited early pressure, allowing the leader to dictate terms through steady fractions. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace early and avoid the tactical complications that will face hold-up horses in a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Wonderful Wendy gets an easy lead and isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: She can dictate comfortable fractions and prove hard to peg back despite her modest ability level. The lack of early pace pressure allows her to save energy for a strong finish when others are struggling to make up ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Electric Bass or Port Of Entry can sit in the perfect stalking position behind the leader
scenarios.body: They get the ideal trip tracking the moderate pace before striking in the final two furlongs. Their superior ratings over the leader become decisive when they inherit the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes crawling slow
scenarios.body: Cloudside Rock or Bug Boy get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kick from the back. The extreme tactical nature allows them to overcome their poor positioning and win on pure ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Big Win Forward Move
scenarios.trigger: If Big Win presses the leader early and creates genuine pace pressure
scenarios.body: His strong recent form and prominent style allows him to wear down Wonderful Wendy in a genuine gallop. The increased tempo plays into his hands as a horse with tactical speed.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Wonderful Wendy gets pressured early by Big Win or Electric Bass as she may not handle competition for the lead
Monitor the pace through the first half-mile as an overly slow tempo will significantly favour the hold-up horses
Bug Boy and Cloudside Rock need to be positioned closer than usual given the likely lack of pace pressure
Electric Bass has never won in 14 starts so watch for any sign of stopping when hitting the front
Track conditions favor horses with proven soft ground form, particularly Bug Boy and Cloudside Rock
